text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 2.5% today, extending a two-week decline of 14%, as oil prices weakened and refinery margins compressed. US crude dropped below $82 per barrel while refining capacity remains high at 95.7%, leaving less room for profitable processing spreads—the difference between what refiners can sell refined products for versus the cost of crude input. Inventories of gasoline and diesel are ample, adding further pressure on margins and limiting upside for a refiner in this environment.

The broader headwind is geopolitical uncertainty without a clear oil supply shock: while tensions in the Middle East have flared (the Kuwait incident), Trump's rhetoric about controlling the conflict's pace suggests markets aren't pricing in a sustained supply disruption. Meanwhile, the failed climate talks at COP31 removed any near-term risk of fossil-fuel restrictions, but also removed a potential "risk premium" that might have supported energy prices. MPC is caught in a low-price, high-capacity squeeze with no near-term catalyst.
